verdict.rationale: GitLab documents on-demand security scans, downloadable scan results in Ultimate, and automatic false-positive detection with confidence scores, which together cover parts of the story. An official CLI exists, but nothing shows it triggering scans headlessly, the results being in a machine-readable format, or issues being filed from findings. missing for 10: evidence that the CLI can trigger scans headlessly, a documented machine-readable result format for agent parsing, a documented workflow for filing issues from findings, and hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can have an agent run a scan headlessly via the CLI, parse machine-readable results, and file issues for real findings

citations.quote: you can run security scans on demand, or schedule them to run at regular intervals
In Ultimate, you can also download the security scan results
false positive detection runs automatically after each security scan and provides confidence scores with explanations for each assessment
